facts.claim: "Girl Like Me" was released on December 9, 2022 as a single on Disruptor Records/Columbia Records, and runs 2:29.
The song was written by Dove Cameron, Edwyn Collins, Evan Blair and Lowell, and produced by Evan Blair.
The track interpolates or samples Edwyn Collins' "A Girl Like You", flipping its perspective. Cameron said she "rewrote" the 1994 hit.
Cameron said the song was inspired by Demi Moore's villain scene in Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle (2003), where "A Girl Like You" plays.
Cameron told People she had loved "A Girl Like You" for about 15 years. She first thought of covering it on tour, then decided to flip the narrative to "have you ever met a girl like me before".
Cameron performed the song for the first time at iHeartRadio 102.7 KIIS FM's Jingle Ball in Los Angeles on December 2, 2022.
Cameron first teased the song on TikTok in March 2022.
Press described the track as a sultry, fast-paced pop anthem. The electric guitar enters after the first chorus.
In the singles chronology, "Girl Like Me" follows "Bad Idea" (Oct 2022), which Evan Blair also produced. Blair also produced her earlier singles "Boyfriend" and "Breakfast".
Cameron first rose to fame on the Disney Channel. Her solo EP "Bloodshot/Waste" came out in September 2019, and "Boyfriend" (2022) hit number 12 on the Billboard Hot 100.

research.lineage: A 2020s alt-pop/pop-rock single that reworks Edwyn Collins' 1994 post-punk-tinged hit "A Girl Like You" with a flipped, femme-fatale perspective.

draft:
The chorus of **Girl Like Me** keeps tripping before the last word. "Never met a girl like, never met a girl like," again and again, the sentence cut off right where the boast should land, and "me" doesn't arrive until the song's final line. The tease is built into the grammar. Dove Cameron spends two and a half minutes describing herself to a man and won't finish the description until she's done with him.

The bones come from Edwyn Collins' 1994 hit "A Girl Like You," and Collins shares the writing credit with Cameron, Evan Blair and Lowell. Cameron said she'd loved that song for about 15 years and first thought of covering it on tour, then decided to flip it so the question became "have you ever met a girl like me before." The spark was a specific image: Demi Moore's villain scene in *Charlie's Angels: Full Throttle*, where the Collins song plays. That tells you the stance. Collins sang about the girl. Cameron answers as the girl, and she plays her as the villain who knows the camera is on her.

The verses are pure taunt. "Nothing makes you smaller, than being a big man" is the sharpest line here, an insult built as a neat little paradox. She calls him heathen and handsome like pet names with a blade in them, mocks his tantrum, and leads him through the dance while asking if a woman has ever been allowed to do that. Then one line slips sideways: "And I'm not even here I'm just a phantom." It comes tossed off between jabs, and it lets in a cold draft. The power she's describing might belong to a character more than a person, a role worn so well that whoever's inside it half vanishes. The song never stops to sort that out. Contempt, appetite and a flicker of absence share the same verse, and the swagger holds.

Blair, who also produced "Bad Idea," "Boyfriend" and "Breakfast," frames it in glossy, driving pop: four-on-the-floor kick and snare with ticking hi-hats, synth bass, a sustained pad, and a plucked arpeggiated figure that keeps everything leaning forward. After the first chorus a distorted electric guitar comes in with long held notes, a rougher edge for a song built on a '90s rock hit. Cameron's voice is clear and bright, the delivery clipped and rhythmic, sliding toward speech in spots, while stacked harmonies swell into something close to a choir at her back. The mix is open and reverberant, like a big stage with the lights down.

The stutter is clever for a long time, and it runs a little long by the last pile-up of repeats.

What sticks is the withheld word: you spend the whole song waiting for her to say "me," and by the time she does, you've already agreed.

factCheck.note: The line "You've never met a girl like me before" says "me" in the chorus. Only the stuttering repeats are cut off, and the final line is the one that ends on "me". The opening and closing sentences were rewritten to match.
